author_or_org: Alireza Rezazadeh, Zichao Li, Ange Lou, Yuying Zhao, Wei Wei, Yujia Bao

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Persistent memory has been shown to enhance single-agent performance, but most approaches assume a monolithic, single-user context and overlook knowledge transfer across users under dynamic, asymmetric permissions.
claims.quote: While persistent memory has been shown to enhance single-agent performance, most approaches assume a monolithic, single-user context-overlooking the benefits and challenges of knowledge transfer across users under dynamic, asymmetric permissions.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The paper introduces Collaborative Memory, a framework for multi-user, multi-agent environments with asymmetric, time-evolving access controls encoded as bipartite graphs linking users, agents, and resources.
claims.quote: We introduce Collaborative Memory, a framework for multi-user, multi-agent environments with asymmetric, time-evolving access controls encoded as bipartite graphs linking users, agents, and resources.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The system maintains two memory tiers: private memory visible only to the originating user, and shared memory with selectively shared fragments.
claims.quote: Our system maintains two memory tiers: (1) private memory-private fragments visible only to their originating user; and (2) shared memory-selectively shared fragments.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Each memory fragment carries immutable provenance attributes, including contributing agents, accessed resources, and timestamps, to support retrospective permission checks.
claims.quote: Each fragment carries immutable provenance attributes (contributing agents, accessed resources, and timestamps) to support retrospective permission checks.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Granular read policies enforce current user-agent-resource constraints and project existing memory fragments into filtered transformed views.
claims.quote: Granular read policies enforce current user-agent-resource constraints and project existing memory fragments into filtered transformed views.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Write policies determine fragment retention and sharing, applying context-aware transformations to update the memory.
claims.quote: Write policies determine fragment retention and sharing, applying context-aware transformations to update the memory.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The framework claims safe, efficient, and interpretable cross-user knowledge sharing, with provable adherence to asymmetric, time-varying policies and full auditability of memory operations.
claims.quote: Our framework enables safe, efficient, and interpretable cross-user knowledge sharing, with provable adherence to asymmetric, time-varying policies and full auditability of memory operations.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The read and write policies may be designed conditioned on system, agent, and user-level information.
claims.quote: Both policies may be designed conditioned on system, agent, and user-level information.
